hints: Apply Newton's second law along the slope: $DF - R - mg\sin 4^\circ = ma$.
Use $P = DF \times v$ with $P = 30000\text{ W}$ to solve for the speed $v$.
walkthrough:
State Newton's second law for motion parallel to the inclined plane (taking uphill as positive):
$$\Sigma F = ma \implies DF - mg\sin 4^\circ - R = ma$$
where $DF$ is the driving force, $R = 1550\text{ N}$ is the resistance, $m = 1400\text{ kg}$, and $a = 0.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

Calculate each term with $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
- Gravity component: $mg\sin 4^\circ = 1400 \times 10 \times \sin 4^\circ = 14000 \times 0.0697565 = 976.591\text{ N}$.
- Net force requirement: $ma = 1400 \times 0.4 = 560\text{ N}$.

Solve for the driving force $DF$:
$$DF = ma + R + mg\sin 4^\circ$$
$$DF = 560 + 1550 + 976.591 = 3086.591\text{ N}$$

State the formula relating power, driving force, and speed:
$$P = DF \times v \implies v = \frac{P}{DF}$$
Substitute $P = 30\text{ kW} = 30000\text{ W}$ and $DF = 3086.591\text{ N}$:
$$v = \frac{30000}{3086.591} \approx 9.71946\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $v = 9.72\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

hints: At the maximum constant speed of $40\text{ m s}^{-1}$, the acceleration is zero.
The driving force must balance the resistance and the downhill component of weight: $DF = R + mg\sin 4^\circ$.
Multiply $DF$ by $40\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find the maximum engine power.
walkthrough:
State the equilibrium condition along the incline for maximum constant speed ($a = 0$):
$$\Sigma F = 0 \implies DF - mg\sin 4^\circ - R = 0$$
$$DF = mg\sin 4^\circ + R$$

Calculate the driving force required:
$$mg\sin 4^\circ = 1400 \times 10 \times \sin 4^\circ \approx 976.591\text{ N}$$
$$R = 1550\text{ N}$$
$$DF = 976.591 + 1550 = 2526.591\text{ N}$$

Calculate the maximum power output using $P = DF \times v$ with $v = 40\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P_{\text{max}} = 2526.591 \times 40 = 101063.64\text{ W}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $101000\text{ W}$ (or $101\text{ kW}$).
